- Military Times, 22 hours ago: Army sets date, location for execution of Nidal Malik Hasan.
The execution by firing squad of Hasan is scheduled for Dec. 3 at Fort Hood, the same location where the former Army officer killed 13 and wounded 32.

81 U.S. military aircraft have been lost or damaged in Operation Epic Fury, according to the Congressional Research Service.
- Military Times, 22 hours ago: Latest AH-64 Apache grounding likely to last months, officials say.
An order to ground hundreds of the Army’s AH-64E Apache attack helicopters is likely to affect every squadron and is expected to be in place for months.
The Caribbean - bottom line: ‘Cushy office’ scale down - Civil society advocates question Gov’t decision-making as backlash leads to pull back on NaRRA office space . PM warns adjustment will slow roll-out of projects, impact delivery.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: ‘Cushy office’ scale down - Civil society advocates question Gov’t decision-making as backlash leads to pull back on NaRRA office space . PM warns adjustment will slow roll-out of projects, impact delivery.
The Government’s decision to scale down the office space that will house the National Reconstruction and Resilience Authority (NaRRA) and cut rental costs, though welcomed, is raising questions about the quality of analysis behind government lease agreements, civil society advocate Carol Narcisse has said. “The decision-making clearly has to be more thoughtful about identifying needs and making sure that what we are expending is commensurate with what is needed and what is sufficient,” Narcisse told The Gleaner yesterday.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Walk for the Cure returns amid mammography crisis.
Jamaicans are being urged to turn cancer awareness into action by participating in the 15th staging of CIBC Caribbean’s Walk for the Cure at Hope Botanical Gardens on Sunday. The event, being held in partnership with the Jamaica Cancer Society (JCS), comes as the society faces an urgent need for more than $35 million to replace its only mammogram machine, which has been out of service since August 29. The 2026 staging is being held under the theme ‘One Caribbean. One Mission. Communities Walking for Change’, with a focus on cancer awareness, screening, treatment and care.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Ali warns Caribbean to scale up or risk being left behind.
GEORGETOWN, Guyana: Guyana’s President Dr Mohamed Irfaan Ali has warned Caribbean tourism leaders to “scale up” or risk being left behind as destinations in the Middle East and Latin America pour billions into tourism infrastructure and development. Ali said the Caribbean could no longer depend primarily on its beaches, natural beauty and established global appeal, arguing that the next phase of tourism must be driven by larger and smarter investments in transportation, resilience, technology, visitor experiences and regional integration.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

- AllAfrica - Conflict, 7 hours ago: Ethiopia: Eritrean Troops Reportedly Deploy in Tigray As Tension With Ethiopia Escalate.

[Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- Renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia has marked a serious escalation since the November 2022 Pretoria Agreement, which ended the two-year war between the federal government and the Tigray region. The renewed hostilities have affected parts of Tigray, Amhara and Afar regions, with reports of damage to civilian property and public institutions, particularly in Tigray.

[The Conversation Africa] In southern Africa, the El Niño - caused by warmer sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean which affect air pressure and wind directions - usually brings below-average summer rainfall and increases the risk of drought. This means poor harvests of maize, a staple crop for many countries on the continent.

The Iran-backed Houthis have claimed a wave of attacks on Saudi civilian infrastructure in recent weeks, which came as Riyadh-backed forces pressed a counteroffensive against the group’s territorial gains. The two countries have been at loggerheads since Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky last month disclosed the prisoner transfer, sparking anger in Seoul, which said it had placed their families in North Korea at risk. South Asia - bottom line: Drones, explosions and soldiers in bulldozers: Surrounded by Israelis in Lebanon's 'model town'.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Drones, explosions and soldiers in bulldozers: Surrounded by Israelis in Lebanon's 'model town'.
Dodging the broken glass carpeting her home in southern Lebanon, Mariam al-Yaghi exited onto her upper balcony and pointed. A few hundred metres ​away was a sight the 67-year-old had grown accustomed to: military vehicles moving through the adjacent Lebanese village, still occupied by Israeli troops. Mariam al-Yaghi ,67, Lebanese resident from West Zawtar, stands in her damaged house in southern Lebanon, on October 1, 2026. — Reuters At night, Israeli soldiers patrol so close to Yaghi’s home in ‌West Zawtar that she can hear their voices.
- Dawn (Pakistan), just now: Bahrain working to 'speed up' approval of Pak-GCC free trade pact, foreign minister says.
Bahrain on Thursday said it was working to “speed up” the approval of a free trade agreement between Pakistan and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC). The remarks came after the two countries held the third session of their Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC) in Islamabad. Bahrain’s FM Abdullatif bin Rashid Al Zayani — who arrived in Pakistan last night on a two-day visit — co-chaired the JMC session along with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. Addressing a joint press briefing with Dar, the Bahraini minister noted that the JMC meeting covered “more than 15 fields”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: 9 terrorists killed in North Waziristan IBO: state media.
Security forces killed nine terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan, state media reported on Wednesday. According to state-run Pakistan TV, IBOs were carried out in several areas of North Waziristan, including Palangzai, Nadeem Kot, and Kot Khazri, eliminating nine Fitna al-Khwarij terrorists, including four “important terrorist commanders”. Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).
- Dawn (Pakistan), The Hindu - International, South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: Trump says he deserves Nobel Peace Prize but has doubts he will get it.
US President Donald Trump, who waged war with Iran and has yet to broker peace in Ukraine, said on Wednesday that he should win the Nobel Peace Prize but acknowledged doubt about his chances. “I don’t know what their decision is going to be,” Trump said of the 2026 award, which the Norwegian Nobel Committee will announce on Friday. “They have a reputation for maybe not giving it to people like me.” Since his return to the White House last year, Trump has repeatedly said he deserves what may be the world’s most prestigious award. “It is about that time,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.
India - bottom line: At 94, Indian Air Force is looking beyond fighter jets: What comes next.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: At 94, Indian Air Force is looking beyond fighter jets: What comes next.
The Indian Air Force marked its 94th anniversary, emphasizing its growth since 1932. Air Chief highlighted the significance of training and readiness, as showcased in various exercises this year. Technologies such as artificial intelligence and autonomous systems are shaping modern warfare and enhancing decision-making. The IAF's self-reliance strategy promotes development of indigenous aircraft and missile systems. Coordination between the IAF, Army, and Navy is increasing, demonstrating integration in national defense.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: The skies have changed, so has IAF's mission: 94 years of India's air power.
Raised on 8 October 1932, the Indian Air Force began with four Westland Wapiti biplanes and five Indian pilots at Drigh Road, Karachi. Today it is the world's fourth-largest air force, operating fighters such as the Su-30MKI, Rafale and Tejas, though it fields around 29 fighter squadrons against a sanctioned 42. Its combat record spans the Second World War, the wars of 1947-48, 1965 and 1971, Kargil, Balakot and Operation Sindoor.

Cornelia and Richard Thornburgh have successfully sold their prestigious lakefront mansion on Everglades Island for an impressive $25.4 million. Initially priced at $24.9 million, the property saw multiple price adjustments before finding a buyer. Acquired by the couple in 2014 for $9 million, they invested significantly in renovations. Following this lucrative sale, they opted for a cozy historic bungalow on Australian Avenue, purchased for $8.12 million.
